version.changelog:
- Added two new phoneme recognizer models (wav2vec2-xlsr-53-espeak and ZIPA-IPA) to ASR, bringing the total bundled ASR slugs to 14.
- Updated documentation to reflect the new phoneme recognition capabilities, which emit IPA phones.
- Removed the skill-card.md file.
- Clarified model lists and endpoints in overview and use-case sections.

llm.summary: This is a coherent speech-service skill, but its documented defaults can expose sensitive audio, files, and server-side network access without enough containment.

dimensions.detail: For a private localhost deployment the capabilities are proportionate, but the default all-interface unauthenticated service is overbroad for an API that processes recordings, transcripts, TTS text, custom voice samples, URL downloads, MCP calls, and file deletion.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Primary Docker examples publish port 8000 on all host interfaces, leave authentication optional by default, mount persistent host data, and use mutable latest/latest-cuda image tags.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill documents high-impact operations such as shared file listing/deletion, persistent staging, server-side URL fetching, and model eviction; it gives agent guardrails, but several risks depend on user/operator discipline rather than enforced scoping.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Staged uploads, cached URL downloads, model data, and custom voice samples persist under the mounted data directory; staged files have no per-caller ownership or automatic expiry and can be listed, read, or deleted by any API caller.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The ASR, TTS, voice-cloning, MCP, URL-fetch, model-management, and file-staging features fit the stated self-hosted speech-service purpose and are substantially disclosed.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only for a trusted self-hosted Talkies instance. Bind to localhost or a protected network, set TALKIES_AUTH_TOKEN, enable TALKIES_BLOCK_PRIVATE_DOWNLOADS before accepting untrusted callers, avoid staging sensitive media on shared instances, clean up staged files and custom voices, and prefer pinned image digests over latest tags.
llm.findings:
[TM1] expected: Model unload endpoints are expected resource-management features, and the artifact warns to use them only for explicit maintenance, but they can disrupt concurrent work if exposed without authentication.
[TM1] expected: File deletion is expected for cleanup, but the documented shared staging namespace has no ownership boundary, so an API caller could remove or inspect another caller's staged files.
[E1] expected: Sending audio, TTS text, and MCP requests to TALKIES_URL is core to the skill and is repeatedly disclosed; this is not hidden exfiltration, but users must trust the configured server.
[E1] expected: Uploading files and using file_path URLs are expected workflow features, but server-side downloads are cached persistently and later readable through the shared files API.
[RP1] unexpected: Running a container is expected for setup, but mutable latest/latest-cuda tags are not necessary and weaken supply-chain reviewability.
[EA2] expected: The scanner hit voice-cloning language that is actually an acceptable-use warning requiring consent; this supports disclosure rather than autonomous abuse.
[RA2] expected: Persistent custom voice directories are expected for reusable voices, but voice samples and transcripts are sensitive and need explicit retention control.
[T09] expected: Server-side URL fetching is a documented feature, but private-network blocking defaults to false, creating SSRF risk on deployments reachable by untrusted callers.
[T05] unexpected: The documented quick-install path combines all-interface port publishing with no default auth, giving reachable callers broad API authority unless the operator hardens it.
[T05] unexpected: The shared persistent file-staging API lacks object-level authorization; the artifact discloses this, but disclosure does not prevent cross-caller read/delete abuse.
[T08] unexpected: The installation examples use mutable third-party container tags, so future installs may run code different from the reviewed artifact.
